notes.title: Mother Machine Update 1.3.1
notes.content:
Today's patch fixes a few issues that some players have reported:

Fixed crash on startup when using FSR on some GPUs
Fixed crash when completing some Adventures
Fixed being able to take damage while still in the loading screen (and then getting stuck in loading)


Thanks for your bug reports! Use the in-game bug reporter where possible to report issues.

notes.title: Mother Machine Update 1.3
notes.content:
Greetings Gremlins,

Today's update brings a long-requested feature to the game: Offline Mode! There's also support for AMD's FSR technologies to get a faster frame-rate, a new Leg-Up ability, and more - here are the full details:


Offline Mode: You can now play Mother Machine without an internet connection! If you want to force the game to always play offline, there's a new option in the game settings. And if you can't connect to the shared Mother's Home but otherwise are online, you can still play the game and join your friends in the Caves as normal.
Leg-Up Ability:  Hold the Climb button without moving to offer a leg-up to your fellow Gremlins. They can then jump higher with your assistance!
FSR Support: The game now supports AMD's FSR technologies, both for Upscaling and Frame Generation.  New Cosmetics: There are a number of new cosmetic options and emotes to unlock.
Bug Fixes: This update includes a number of fixes for bugs, including jerky climbing, unwanted falling off ropes, getting stuck in the floor, and many more.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/f28a4cd19ea31ac5689f915e4fca8861d3ca609e.gif"]The team at Maschinen-Mensch wants to thank all of you wonderful Gremlins who have been enjoying the game since we launched it earler this year. If you've been having fun in the caves, a Steam review would mean the world to us - it's how other Gremlins find their way to Mother Machine!

notes.title: Mother Machine Update 1.2.1
notes.content:
Greetings Gremlins,

We hope you're enjoying exploring the Creators' Ruins! Today's update has a few fixes for Split Screen and Steam Deck:

Fixed Player 2 not having correct interaction prompts sometimes in splitscreen

Fixed Player 2 not being able to leave menus when using the "P1 Uses Controller" mode

Removed the "Fullscreen" option on Steam Deck that caused issues (use "Windowed Fullscreen" instead)

The onscreen keyboard is now displayed as appropriate when sending a bug report on Steam Deck

Increased the size of some input prompts so they are properly readable on Steam Deck

notes.title: Mother Machine Update 1.2 (Creators' Ruins Update)
notes.content:
As well as the new Creators' Ruins Biome (plus 10 new mutations!), this update has a number of bug fixes and other changes. In particular, we've made some big improvements to the performance of the game which should now run at a higher framerate, both on lower spec machines and those with the newest GPUs!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/dc79db6f1d1fe887ba1ecb175010b0e7c0fe4769.gif

NEW
Added the Creators' Ruins Biome (click here for more details)
Added new Platforms to start Creators' Ruins expeditions in the bottom of Mother's Home
Added 10 new Mutations unlockable with Radberries found in Creators' Ruins
Steam Remote Play Together is now supported (if you have problems, try running the game in Fullscreen mode, not Windowed Fullscreen)
CHANGED
The Adventures "TOTAL EXTRACTION" and "THE SECRET PLAN" now take place in the Creators' Ruins
The devices that provide rewards when a battery is inserted now have a new look
Airlocks now have two reward options to choose from (but still only one battery)
Expedition types you haven't yet unlocked can still be played via the Quick Play terminal
Defeating a boss will now display a notification for all players
FIXES
More optimizations: CPU, GPU, and reduced Disk Space usage
Fixed issues when joining caves that were very recently started or finished
Fixed friend invitations not working sometimes
Fixed various input issues in Splitscreen when the setting "P1 Uses Keyboard" is on
When doing a pullup to a narrow ledge, you no longer fall off the other side
Fixed getting multiple "Objective Complete" notifications when only one objective was completed
Fixed various situations where you would be unable to move or perform actions
Fixed issues where the wrong interaction would be triggered while you were holding an item

notes.title: New FREE DLC Incoming: The Creators' Ruins!
notes.content:
Being the chaotic gremlins we are, we're thrilled to announce a huge, lifetime-free Biome DLC for your ultimate enjoyment! Gather your friends and prepare for mayhem: the Creators' Ruins are waiting to be explored (and most likely wrecked) by you!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/09ad11e9a0489b32508224c519c84ad2ef4c9a98.jpg

The Creators' Ruins seamlessly extends the base game of Mother Machine with an array of exciting new features:

10 New Mutations
Unlock even more special Mutations to expand your gameplay abilities! Steal health with the Vampire Attack, or morph into a ball to roll through the caves, allowing your siblings to carry and throw you around. Become the ninja gremlin you always dreamed of with the Chameleon Skin, or unleash electric shockwaves with a well-timed fart. And many more!

Elektro Chomper Boss
Brace yourself for thrilling new boss encounters against the colossal Elektro Chomper. Beware of its powerful electric attacks—they are shockingly effective!

Rogue Drones
Ancient Colonist Technology remains active within the Ruins, and unfortunately, it decided that you are a trespasser! Prepare for a constant barrage of hostile Rogue Drones.

Mini Hoppers
A new breed of miniature Mini Hoppers has been spotted in the Creators' Ruins Biome. While not dangerous individually, they appear in massive groups and will surely create pure chaos with their frenetic jumping behavior.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/68c6f3bc236ab6d0f267c65aefb11ff5564d16dd.gif

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We can't wait for you to dive into the Creators' Ruins and experience all the new chaos! What part of this update are you most excited to try first?

notes.title: Mother Machine Update 1.0.2
notes.content:
Greetings Gremlins!

Today's update adds support for DLSS technologies and also gives you more control over how some of the graphics options behave. We know many of you woud like the game to run at a higher frame-rate, and this is just the first step to making that happen. We are focusing on optimizing the game, both in terms of rendering performance and also the overhead of managing everything that's going on in the cave for devices with less powerful CPUs (looking at you, Steam Deck!).

There are also a few tuning changes and of course bug fixes in this update. We've seen that the platform next to Mother (we call it the Quick Play Platform) can be a bit confusing for new players, and we have some larger changes in the works for improving how you get into caves quickly. In the meantime though, we've changed the display above the platform to show the player count, to make it clearer you are joining a cave that has other players in it. We've also added a way of inviting friends into caves with a single press, with a new button in the corner.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/613068eb21419efd8a6ddb518f27633edef023bd.png

Don't forget that the Misty Grove DLC is free for another week! It gives you access to a whole new Biome with different creatures, a new Boss, and 10 unique mutations to unlock. If you own it, Mother will give you a little introduction next time you visit her Home - and if not, the game will now remind you to claim it for free!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3357220/Mother_Machine__Misty_Grove/

We have much more planned for Mother Machine (including new content!), but our focus right now is improving performance and fixing more bugs, so expect more updates in the coming weeks! In the meantime, if you've been enjoying the game, please do leave a review on Steam. Now, on to the full details:

Full Patch Notes:

NEW
Added options for controlling the upscaling method and amount of upscaling:
  Auto: Will select the based option based on your hardware and Graphics mode
  Built-In: Uses Unreal's upscaling method. You can select the percentage of upscaling, or turn it off completely.
  DLSS-SR (requires NVIDIA RTX GPU): Uses NVDIA's Deep Learning Super Sampling - Super Resolution method. You can control the amount of upscaling from DLAA (no upscaling, AA only) to UltraPerformance (maximum upscaling)
  NVIDIA NIS: Uses NVIDIA Imagine Scaling method. This is compatible with non-NVIDIA GPUs. You can control the amount of upscaling from UltraQuality (minimum upscaling) to Performance (maximum upscaling)  
Added support for DLSS Frame Generation technologies (requires NVIDIA RTX 40 series or better GPU). You can control the amount of frame generation based on what your hardware supports, or turn it off.
Added support for limiting the frame rate. You can choose 30, 60 or Unlimited.
Added a quick way to invite a friend into a cave: look in the top-left of the screen to see how. Note this only appears when the cave isn't full!
Mother will now give you an introduction to the Misty Grove if you have the DLC. If you don't have the DLC, it's free! The game will also remind you to claim it.
CHANGED
Tutorial: Removed the laser gate
Tutorial: added an automatically created portal if you don't do it
Tutorial: When Mother tells you to step on the plate, you stop to listen
The Sinister Sister: Added more crystals & food
Map: Increased the radius of the "hint" map area as you explore
Cave Harvest: improved textures on the Shredder
Perk Pills that you get from Boxes now display their perk description when you are near them
You can now access Custom Expeditions immediately after finishing the tutorial
The Quick Play platform (the one by Mother) now displays the number of players in the cave instead of the Exploration %
FIXED
Fixed trampoline platforms sometimes being hard to get on (or them throwing you off)
Fixed Balloons sometimes getting stuck in the walls
Fixed Portals not working sometimes
Fixed some issues with spectating other players
Fixed getting stuck when doing an emote while going through a door
Fixed Gentle Giant showing acid splashes when not in acid
Fixed Drown in Acid achievement not properly unlocking
Fixed large creatures not moving sometimes
Fixed the death sound playing when players leave Mother's Home
Fixed caves generating sometimes with battery-powered beam gates that you might not have a battery for
We're still looking into the crash some players experience when accessing the mutations menu. In the meantime, you can use the Launch Option "-DisableMediaPlayer" to prevent the crash.

notes.title: The Art of Chaos
notes.content:
About Mother Machine
After working for 10 years on games that rely heavily on procedural generation, we are about to release our latest game, Mother Machine, on March 26th. Unlike our previous games, which were tile-based strategy games, Mother Machine is a 2.5D multiplayer platformer with a strong emphasis on exploration.

It’s pretty wild when you think about the shift in genre, but I was eager to apply our knowledge of procedural generation to the more immediate, physical gameplay that platformers offer. At its core, Mother Machine still shares a lot with the Curious Expedition games we've made before. You explore a procedurally generated world filled with obstacles, dangers, and rewards to overcome. We also wanted to keep the gameplay loop short and engaging, structuring it around runs that provide a satisfying experience within 15 to 30 minutes.

From the very beginning, we knew we would once again rely heavily on a sophisticated procedural world generation system to create an extremely replayable game structure. However, this time, players will use the roguelite repetition to master their platforming abilities and experiment with mutations, special active abilities that let them personalize their movement and define their role in a multiplayer group.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/1f343a1d5dc1d017edd2966ef4142d1ec2d12812.gif

With this article, I'm trying to give a not-too-technical overview of how our procedural generation is set up. Bear in mind that I'm not a programmer—my role in procedural generation has always been to focus on conceptual design and then tune and balance the systems. There’s a huge part of the coding side missing from this, but it would take my partner in procedural crime, Isaac Ashdown, the technical director of Mother Machine, to write that part.

I would like to give a shoutout to Derek Yu’s Spelunky and Darius Kazemi’s Spelunky Generator Lessons, which were, of course, very influential in shaping the initial starting points of our procedural design.

From Splines to Chunks
Since our game revolves around exploring the caves of an alien planet, we refer to our levels as "caves." A cave typically has a starting and ending point and follows a mostly sequential structure. However, we incorporate branching paths and loops that can reconnect different routes. The structure of a cave also varies depending on its goal type. There are six different goal types in the shipping version of the game. For now, I'll keep things simple, as these aspects are not essential to explaining the procedural setup.

The basic building blocks of our caves are called "chunks." A chunk is a hand-designed piece, similar to a puzzle piece, that contains a set number of what we call "anchors." These anchors allow chunks to connect seamlessly to other chunks with matching anchors.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/b82052ac4d2c7d8264cf8d18f775bb8002b74e8a.gif

Chunks are created by drawing simple splines in the Unreal Editor. This approach allows us to achieve organic shapes, long slopes, rounded corners, and other features that would be difficult to create using pre-made building blocks. Another advantage of using splines to define the shape is the ability to iterate quickly on the geometry. Adjusting the 2D spline and hitting play instantly updates the level, making it easy to test how the shape interacts with gameplay mechanics and how it feels spatially, an aspect I care a lot about.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/709b6ca9da325a1a7c1cfce715394c71d146e9b2.gif

Another advantage of using splines is that they allow us to generate any type of geometry. This means that all designed chunks can be used in any biome of the game. As a result, creating additional chunks benefits all biomes, regardless of when they are released.

The process of generating 3D geometry from a 2D spline is a complex topic that could easily warrant its own in-depth article. In short, we use Houdini, a powerful node-based 3D tool by SideFX, to handle this process. Specifically, we integrate it as an Unreal plugin, the Houdini Engine, where we feed in the 2D spline along with anchors and some additional meta-information. Houdini then runs in the background, without the level designer ever needing to open the tool, calculating the 3D geometry and updating it in the engine almost instantly.

The instant part refers to the simple greybox geometry, while the more complex biome-specific geometry requires significantly more computational power and is processed offline on a dedicated server.
Additionally, we use Unreal's PCG system to place foliage on the generated geometry, but diving deeper into that would go beyond the scope of this article. Here’s an example of how a chunk spline is used to generate three different types of geometry:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/44b3371a14344faad4cbd586ffc9bacae22fa848.png

Okay, back to chunks and how they are stitched together!

Even though I follow a minimum grid of 50 Unreal Units (UU) when designing splines, it isn't strictly necessary for the internal shape of a chunk. However, I still adhere to it for easier debugging, maintaining repeatable patterns, and simplifying distance measurements for jumps and other gameplay elements.

What does need to align with a grid is the position of the anchors and the outer shell of a chunk. Specifically, these elements must follow a 1000UU grid to ensure that chunks connect seamlessly without clipping into each other. This 1000UU grid is what we refer to as our "base grid."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/8e7d01cb0ef5662d383c7f8b8bedb1b1e5049e7a.png

Each anchor must always be placed precisely in the center of the base grid's outline and must maintain a distance of 300UU from the surrounding geometry on each side. This ensures that passages between chunks are standardized, consistently measuring 6 meters, and function seamlessly across all chunk designs.

There are actually two types of anchors: normal and wide. The wide variant allows for larger openings between chunks. However, for the sake of simplicity in this article, I will focus only on normal anchors.

Here's a small selection of different chunks. As you can see, they come in various shapes, sizes, and anchor positions. However, the outer shells and the placement of the anchors always conform to the base grid.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/3e47230a2e5b85cdac8475b30b899afe00f05690.png

There are various sizes of chunks, each with a different number of anchors. They are categorized by usage types, such as "connector" (which usually has only a few anchors), "hall" (which typically has wider openings and higher ceilings), "mini" (the smallest possible chunks, measuring 1000UU x 1000UU, or 10 meters x 10 meters, the base grid size), and "deadend" (which have only one anchor). However, these names do not influence how the procedural system uses the chunks, they simply help me keep an overview. In total, we will be shipping the game with 496 different chunks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/b222c0ee56ba6d817b0d117ad49fce5dd5afed57.png

Cave Generation

When a cave is generated, the system aims to reach a specific "path length." One unit of path length corresponds to the size of our base grid. The path length is determined by the cave generation setup, which I'll discuss later. For now, here’s an example of how a simple cave typically looks.

At the top, you can see a simplified debug version, which we call the "cave explorer," while the bottom shows a zoomed-out view of the actual gameplay geometry. In the cave explorer, you’ll notice colored dots representing the positions of all chunk anchors.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/3e7b059ebb9dcede4c549317e1037cbf74f93e55.png

This example cave is made up almost entirely of "mini" chunks and has a path length of 50. The path concludes with a large hall chunk, which serves as the standard goal area for our caves.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/c5991d5c7b550ed5c7f9e8bbfff93bf3ed8d9aaf.png

The exact length of a cave and the selection of chunks along its path depend on two key factors: "chunk sets" and "sections."

A chunk set is a collection of different chunks that are randomly selected when the system places a chunk.
A section, on the other hand, is the core of cave generation design. It defines several important parameters, including:

 Which chunk set is used
 The path length for this section
 The types of gameplay actors that spawn
 Which anchor directions are allowed or excluded
 The mood of the section (which determines color and lighting settings)


This example shows a very simple section. It has a path length of 10, uses the "Small Halls" chunk set, and spawns a few "gumba" enemies, our internal name for a basic enemy type:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/252ac2ab7ec6ced9cf71932a0afdb5c0998e0fde.png

This is what the generation of this section looks like in practice. Note that the cave itself doesn’t have a defined end section, so it simply stops. The emojis you see in the debug display indicate where enemies and other cave objects are placed (the pig icons represent basic enemies).

Also, notice how this cave setup never requires players to pass through an upward anchor while following the main path. This is because the section setup forbids upward anchors. Since upward traversal is generally more difficult in gameplay, we’ve excluded them from this example to keep movement smoother and more accessible.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/892b976722c4cab034469585aa2ca49d7e1292c6.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/4f7f1d9ef21f0cacaeebf0c4dbb36818b31ed17c.png

Here are a few variations of how this section can be generated. Each one maintains an exact path length of 10 and ensures that players never have to traverse an upward anchor connection.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/202ec338d322285ad773413e31d74d247ff18b1b.gif

The example section used the chunk set "small halls." Only the chunks included in this set can be placed when generating the section. Here, you can see the chunks that belong to the small halls chunk set:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/aeee80a7faeb68ef2e824ea5f8f3891f2635c189.png

For reference, this is how the section setup for the much more complex goal-type "cave trek" looks in the shipped version of the game. The branching paths represent the different supported difficulty levels: easy, normal, and hard.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/f11de66f09d608cee663c282d17905cabbcbd7da.png

Here, you can see how the generation places each chunk step by step for a normal difficulty cave.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/26f57ee4a77ce04cf0f9d53dac41f1d408c03fc8.gif

And here are some generation results from the same setup, this time using the hard difficulty:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/de06bc1f168027cb245c3fe4b39607ad3804d0d1.gif

Gameplay Actor Placement

Now let's talk about how our gameplay actors, such as enemies, resources or other interactive things are placed inside chunks. Whenever a chunk is created or adjusted, the system will automatically place "sockets", approximately one socket every meter along the spline. For each socket, a couple of measurements are made to define different tags, such as:

 Is the socket on the top of a spline, the side or the underside?
 When shooting a ray away from the surface the socket is located on, how long will it travel before it hits another spline? This defines the height of the socket
 What are the neighbor sockets?
 Which "ribbon" is the socket located on? There are 3 ribbons in our game which define in which depth an object exists:

 Player Path is the pink ribbon on which the player will move
 FrontPath is in front of the player. Typically we spawn only smaller objects here
 BackPath is behind the player. Here we can spawn larger objects.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/c32c09de7a96a3b4090306e09cf9adfe820b8a57.png

All these values are stored in each socket. When defining a gameplay actor, we can specify which socket requirements the actor must meet to be placed inside a chunk.

For example, our basic enemy has very few placement requirements. It only needs the "Player Path" tag, making it easy to spawn almost anywhere in a chunk.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/5ee450c2d17a1668aa3eb761a54b6a513ab29c5f.png

The acid plant, which drops dangerous acid on players, has much more restrictive placement requirements. It can only be placed on the underside of a spline, as it hangs from the ceiling. Additionally, it requires a height of at least 7 meters (H7) to ensure that the acid drips from a logical height and gives players enough time to react before it reaches them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/93814bd67aaee77ade7f24b2cb6e9ea3a4babe47.gif

To test the placement and requirements of actors within a chunk, we use a special tool called the "theatre." In the theatre, we can specify which chunk is generated and set up a collection of actors to be spawned inside. This is extremely useful for observing the different permutations that a set of actors can take when placed within a chunk in the generated cave.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/de554d80909585b102ad16f128da7e50bf00e305.gif

The theatre can also be used to test an entire section setup instead of just a single chunk. In this case, it generates one permutation of a defined section, as described earlier.

The following example shows multiple generations of a section called "Exploration," a general area that spawns various enemy types, resources, platforming obstacles, and more. This demonstrates how the combination of different chunks from the designated chunk set and the selected gameplay actors creates a wide variety of unique gameplay situations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45146113/d18305092bfbd598ddfc650bf7dc127fad6baff5.gif

Typically, there are many different ways gameplay actors can be spawned within a single chunk. When combined with the fact that the chunk itself is randomly selected from a predefined chunk set, this results in a vast variety of possible combinations within a section.

Conclusion

I hope this article provides some interesting insights and a good, if basic, overview of our procedural generation setup. Having worked on many different procedural systems in the last 10+ years I can proudly say that what we have achieved with Mother Machine is definitely our procedural masterpiece.

For me, it is extremely fulfilling to work on procedural generation. Observing the different outcomes of a growingly complex system is deeply satsfying.

If you want to follow the development of Mother Machine, or support us in developing it please consider wishlisting the game on Steam, this helps us a lot!

Thank you!
Johannes Kristmann

notes.title: Mother Machine Demo Update 2
notes.content:
Hey Gremlins!

Mother Machine's launch is less than 2 weeks away! The team has been hard at work getting the final version ready, and today we're updating the Demo with the new goodies.

As this includes a few balance changes, and changes to the way you progress through the game, we've had to do a progression wipe as part of this update. Don't forget you can skip the tutorial to get straight back into the caves!

Removed the "Glowing Sweat Skin" mutation and replaced it with "Shelled Fart"
After completing the tutorial, you must play a 1-star "Cave Trek" expedition and talk to Mother to unlock the other difficulties and "Pest Control" expedition
Added new customization options and adjusted the prices of some of them
Lots of UI improvements
Improved performance across all graphics modes
Added some more tutorial popups here and there
Lots of bug fixes
Lots of tuning tweaks
Lots of graphical and audio polish


There will be more to come, including more performance updates and missing/improved translations.

For more gremlin news, don't forget to follow our socials and join our discord!
